REPUBLIC OF THE PHILIPPINES DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT Francisco Gold Condominium II EDSA Cor. Mapagmahal St., Diliman Quezon City LEGAL SERVICE BIYAHENG PINOY 2-1 DILG OPINION No. JUN 15 2011 HON. MARIA LEOBETH B. DESI-ATE-DEUCANA, J.D. National President Lady Local Legislators League of the Philippines c/o Office of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan 3rd Floor, Provincial Capitol Bldg. Roxas City 5800 Capiz Dear Hon. Deslate-DeIana: This has reference to your letter dated 13 May 2011 requesting the Department's clarification on whether the Lady Local Legislators League of the Philippines (Four-L Phils.) is considered a government institution so that the limit set by NBC No. 442 as amended by NBC No. 486, which sets the allowable cost of participation of government personnel in conventions, seminars, conferences, symposia and similar gatherings at Php 1,200 per day per participant, is applicable. In reply thereto, please be informed that this Department has been consistent in our opinion that the Local Government Code of 1991 created two (2) kinds of leagues, namely: (I) League of Local Government Units, such as League of Provinces of the Philippines; League of Cities of the Philippines; League of Municipalities of the Philippines; and Liga ng mga Barangay; and (2) League of Elective Officials, such as Municipal Mayors' League, Vice Mayors' League, Vice Governors' League, etc. May we note that in the second kind, local elective officials are allowed to federate themselves into different leagues. In fact, in DILG Opinion No. 41, series of 2006, we already mentioned Four-L as one of those leagues that may be organized by local elective officials. Coming now to the applicability of NBC No. 442 as amended by NBC No. 486, may we note that the DBM has already rendered its opinion on the matter thru a letter dated 16 May 2011 addressed to you, viz: "- National Budget Circular (NBC) No. 442, as amended by NBC No. 486, sets the allowable cost of participation of government personnel in conventions, seminars, conferences, symposia and similar gatherings at Pl,goo per day per participant; any amount in excess of the prescribed rate shall be at the expense of the participant. Such rule applies to activities sponsored by non- government organizations or private institutions in the Philippines. Under Circular Letter No. 10-98, the cost of participation of government personnel in seminars and similar gatherings sponsored by leagues and federations of local government units and local elective officials established pursuant to Republic Act No. 7160 (Local Government Code of 1991) are exempted from the coverage of NBC No. 442. The exemption is an offshoot of the ruling of the Department of Justice that the leagues and federations of local elective officials are to be considered as government institutions/ organiza tions.

In this regard, the Four-L Philippines — being a league of local elective officials—may be considered a government organization. Activities organized by the group shall consequentially be exempted from the coverage of NBC No. 442, as amended. The threshold for participation costs in conventions/ seminars sponsored by the government entities would vary depending on how the gathering is organized. VVhiIe the league should be able to recoup the costs for conducting such seminars/gatherings, these activities should not be viewed as avenues for raising funds, bearing in mind that the participants are government officials/employees. " We have we have addressed your concern accordingly. A Ls/17 Very truly yours, ESUSB OQ Director III
